title: International availability intake: weighted prioritization for sovereignty & failover requests
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Purpose: Define a repeatable intake and weighted scoring system for customer requests that touch region availability, data residency, and failover guarantees. This ticket will produce a single-page triage rubric, an intake form template for Sales/SEs, routing rules for product/infra/legal, and a decision ladder for acceptance vs. negotiated mitigation.

Problem: We receive inconsistent asks from Sales and Support about provisioning in specific geos or offering residency guarantees. Current ad-hoc handling causes long cycles, missed SLAs, and surprise infra work. We need a transparent prioritization method that balances revenue, compliance risk, operational cost, and scalability.

Goals:
- Ship a documented, lightweight scoring rubric used by PM/Sales/SE to triage new requests within 48 hours.
- Reduce time-to-decision for enterprise geo requests from ~4 weeks to <7 business days for clear-pass/clear-deny cases.
- Provide engineering with clear acceptance criteria and guardrails for requests we accept vs. refer to Dedicated/Private options.

Scope:
- Intake fields (customer info, required residency/failover behavior, compliance regimes, revenue, timeline).
- Weighted scoring model with adjustable weights for ARR, legal/regulatory severity, latency/user impact, engineering cost estimate, strategic partnership value.
- Routing rules: immediate Legal review for high-regulatory flags; infra feasibility check for low-latency or low-traffic geos; product & reliability for SLA/failover commitments.
- Triage outputs: Acceptable (go to scoping & roadmap), Mitigatable (requires contract or Dedicated/Private sales), Defer (low-priority backlog), Deny (legal/regulatory blocker).

Non-goals:
- This ticket does not provision regions or change infra automation. It creates the triage tooling and decision logic only.

Stakeholders:
- PM: Marco Alvarez (assignee), Aisha Patel (creator)
- Eng: Runtime & Infra leads (to review acceptance criteria)
- Legal/Privacy: for residency/regulatory gating
- Sales/SE: intake users and requesters
- Customer Success: to surface impact and timeline expectations

Deliverables:
- One-page triage rubric (PDF + Confluence)
- Google Form intake template + Slack intake shortcut for Sales/SE
- Decision ladder flowchart with routing mapping
- Example scoring calculation (spreadsheet) and three annotated examples from recent real requests
- PRD: short doc explaining rollout and governance

Trade-offs discussed:
- Simplicity vs. accuracy: choose a small number (5–6) of weighted factors to keep scoring practical for Sales.
- Revenue vs. compliance: legal severity should veto even high-ARR requests (must be an absolute gating factor).
- Cost modeling: initial engineering cost is estimated via a standard band (low/medium/high) rather than detailed infra quoting to keep triage fast.

Acceptance criteria: [see acceptance_criteria field]
acceptance_criteria: A one-page triage rubric published in Confluence and linked in the Sales playbook
An intake form (Google Form) that captures required fields and produces the weighted score automatically
Routing rules documented: when to call Legal, Eng Runtime, Infra, or Sales Ops
Three historical request examples annotated with final triage outcome and rationale
Stakeholder sign-off: Product, Legal, Runtime eng, Sales Ops
Decision ladder flowchart exported as PNG and embedded in the rubric doc
triage_rubric_summary: Scoring factors (weight in parentheses): ARR (30%), Regulatory severity (absolute veto), Customer criticality / SLA needs (20%), Latency/user locality sensitivity (15%), Engineering cost band (15%), Strategic value/partnership (10%), Time urgency/contract deadline (10%). Regulatory severity when flagged moves issue into Legal review; Legal can mark as 'deny' or 'require mitigations' regardless of score.
intake_fields_template: Primary use-case and data types processed
Regulatory regimes implicated (e.g., GDPR, DPA, sectoral rules)
Technical notes: estimated QPS, model types, latency targets
Preferred solution (hosted, dedicated, private) if known
Legal flags (data residency, export controls, PII/PHI)
routing_rules: If Regulatory severity flagged => route to Legal + Privacy (response SLA 3 business days)
If ARR > $250k and score >= 65 => route to Product Scoping and Infra estimate
If latency sensitivity requires sub-50ms regional nodes => route to Runtime engineering for feasibility evaluation
If customer requests 'data never leaves country' => refer to Private/Dedicated offering and require Sales Ops + Legal scope
If engineering cost band = high and ARR low => recommend Defer and propose alternative (cache/proxy/billed Dedicated)
If time urgency is < 30 days and score borderline => escalate to PM for fast decision; consider short-term mitigations
examples_and_annotation_links: Example A: EU financial customer, ARR $600k, residency required in DE, regulatory severity high => Outcome: Private deployment recommended; Legal required contract clause. (link to annotated case in Drive)
Example B: US consumer app, ARR $40k, latency-sensitive in APAC => Outcome: Acceptable with regional caching + edge routing; infra estimate low. (link to annotated case in Drive)

Example C: Large enterprise, ARR $1.2M, failover SLA requested across EU/US => Outcome: Scoped for Dedicated reserved capacity with canary rollout; Engineering to provide cost table. (link to annotated case in Drive)
risks_and_mitigations: Risk: Overfitting weights that favor near-term revenue => Mitigation: Governance review every quarter with Sales Ops and Finance
Risk: Legal veto delays decision => Mitigation: SLA for Legal triage and pre-baked contract templates for common mitigations
Risk: Engineering underestimates infra work => Mitigation: Standard engineering-cost bands and mandatory infra feasibility gates for accept decisions
Risk: Sales bypassing intake => Mitigation: Automate intake link in CRM/Sales playbook and require intake token before escalation
metrics_and_success_criteria: Median time-to-decision for geo/residency requests reduced from ~22 business days to <= 7 business days for clear cases
% of requests with completed intake form at submission >= 90%
Stakeholder satisfaction: Legal and Runtime average triage confidence >= 4/5 in post-triage survey
% of accepted requests that hit their contractual timelines >= 80% after scoping
dependencies: Runtime eng capacity for feasibility reviews
Template creation in Confluence and Google Drive (Docs/Sheets)
